They contradict the binding foundation pack 8.4 as it stands: the 8091 row says 'mTLS, per-Node enrollment certificate' and the 8092 row says 'mTLS with Ruralz Control peer certificates; Node certificates rejected'. Relays on 8092 are likewise part of the pending OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15 amendment.
blocking.evidence: line 374: "| `Enroll` | Unary | ... | One-time token over TLS with a pinned server CA | Planned (M2) |"; line 382: "8092 is not a public API: it admits only Ruralz Control replicas, relays (Planned (M4)) and the token `Join` of `ruralz control join`"; line 395: "| Control Stream `Enroll` | 8091 | One-time token, pinned server CA |"; line 397: "| Peer layer | 8092 | Peer or relay certificate (mTLS); one-time `admin` token for `Join` |"; pack 8.4: "| 8092 | `ruralz-control` | Raft peer transport ... | mTLS with Ruralz Control peer certificates; Node certificates rejected |"

On lines 382 and 397 add '(pack 8.4 amendment proposed: OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15, OQ-security-and-identity-31)'. Name both IDs in the closing paragraph under Open questions as pending pack amendments this document relies on, so the text reads as a proposal rather than a pack fact.

blocking.section: Ruralz Control REST and gRPC APIs
blocking.issue: The RPC table lists 'Renewal' as a third RPC of `ruralz.control.v1.ControlStream`, with its own 'Node to Ruralz Control and back' shape. Two other documents fix exactly two RPCs, `Enroll` and `Stream`. Release, versioning and compatibility (line 125) says "service `ControlStream`, RPCs `Enroll` and `Stream`", and Repository layout (line 252) says "Service `ControlStream` with unary `Enroll` and bidirectional `Stream`". The `Stream` row's Up list also omits `RenewRequest`, and its Down list omits `RenewResponse`, so the renewal messages belong to no RPC. The API reference is where an implementer reads the RPC set, so this contradiction is blocking.
blocking.evidence: line 375: "| `Stream` | Bidirectional stream | Down: `Snapshot`, `Delta`, `HeartbeatReply`, `TrustUpdate`, `Reconnect`. Up: `Hello`, `Ack`, `Nack`, `Heartbeat` |"; line 376: "| Renewal | Node to Ruralz Control and back | `RenewRequest`, `RenewResponse`, forwarded to the leader | Node certificate | Planned (M2) |"; line 396: "| Control Stream `Stream` and renewal | 8091 |"
blocking.fix: Delete the 'Renewal' row. Add `RenewRequest` to the `Stream` Up list and `RenewResponse` to its Down list, noting 'renewal is forwarded to the leader'. Rename the auth row on line 396 to 'Control Stream `Stream` (including renewal)'. If a separate unary `Renew` RPC is wanted, raise it as an Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops, because release-versioning-and-compatibility and repository-layout-and-conventions would need to change too.

blocking.evidence: line 395: "| Control Stream `Enroll` | 8091 | One-time token, pinned server CA | One Cluster; token consumed | `RZ-CP-001` | Planned (M2) |"; Control plane and GitOps, Control Stream table: "| `EnrollRequest` (RPC `Enroll`) | ... | `EnrollResponse`, `RZ-CP-001` or `RZ-CP-002`; token consumed |"

blocking.section: Ruralz Control REST and gRPC APIs / API authentication
blocking.issue: The document relies on `RZ-CP` codes that do not exist in the registry owned by Control plane and GitOps (RZ-CP-001 to RZ-CP-018). It says a malformed or unknown non-Bundle request field gets "an `RZ-CP` code", but no code covers an invalid request. It also maps every REST API authentication failure to `RZ-CP-007`, which the registry defines as "RBAC or separation-of-duties denial" (an authorization decision), not a missing, expired or invalid session or token.
blocking.evidence: line 365: "unknown request fields are rejected (RZ-CFG-006 for Bundle fields, else an `RZ-CP` code)"; line 393: "| REST API | 8090 | Session cookie (Ruralz Console) or API token ... | ... | `RZ-CP-007`, audited | Planned (M2) |"; Control plane and GitOps API summary: "| RZ-CP-007 | RBAC or separation-of-duties denial |" (no invalid-request or unauthenticated code in RZ-CP-001..018)
blocking.fix: Add an Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops: "Register `RZ-CP` codes for an invalid REST request (unknown or malformed field) and for a failed authentication (missing, expired or revoked session or API token)?", with options (a) two new codes (proposed) or (b) plain 400/401 problem documents without `code`. On line 365, cite it in place of "an `RZ-CP` code". On line 393, write "401 (code: OQ-cli-and-api-surface-8) for failed authentication; `RZ-CP-007` for RBAC or separation-of-duties denials".

blocking.issue: The document says global flags "mean the same in every command" and defines `--token-file PATH` as the "API token for the REST API". `ruralz control join` then reuses `--token-file` for a different credential: the one-time `admin` join token redeemed over the 8092 peer layer. That makes one flag name mean two different things, which contradicts the document's own rule, and a script that sets `--token-file` for REST calls would send its API token to `Join`.
blocking.evidence: line 146: "Flags mean the same in every command."; line 155: "| `--token-file PATH` | API token for the REST API | Same |"; line 138: "| `ruralz control join` | Join a replica to the Raft cluster by redeeming a one-time `admin` token | `--peer HOST:8092`, `--token-file PATH` | Peer layer 8092 `Join` |"
blocking.fix: Rename the `ruralz control join` flag to `--join-token-file PATH` ("one-time join token issued by `/api/v1/replicas`"). Keep `--token-file` for REST API tokens only.

blocking.issue: `ruralz dev run` accepts `--env` and `--environments` and 'launches a local `ruralzd` on a Bundle directory with Hot Reload'. The Configuration model says file-mode `ruralzd` applies no overlay, and OQ-configuration-model-10, which this document says it decides, requires 'no overlay selector in `ruralzd`'. The document never says how the overlay and `spec.variables` reach `ruralzd`. As written, the reader has to assume that `ruralzd` selects an overlay, which contradicts the Configuration model. (`ruralz test run --bundle` does say the Bundle is 'rendered for `--env`'; `ruralz dev run` does not.)
blocking.evidence: line 130: "| `ruralz dev run` | Launch a local `ruralzd` on a Bundle directory with Hot Reload | `[DIR]`, `--env`, `--environments` | Local `ruralzd` | Planned (M1) |"; line 460: "OQ-configuration-model-10 (every listed flag, no overlay selector in `ruralzd`)"; Configuration model, Overlays: "File-mode `ruralzd` applies no overlay; it loads a rendered Bundle or a Revision from an OCI registry (OQ-configuration-model-10)."
blocking.fix: Add one sentence under 'Plugin, AI and development verbs': "With `--env`, `ruralz dev run` renders the Bundle (`ruralz bundle render` semantics) into a private directory, atomically replacing it on every source change, and `ruralzd` watches that rendered one-file Bundle; without `--env`, `ruralzd` watches DIR directly and the process environment supplies `${VAR}`." This keeps `ruralzd` free of an overlay selector.

non_blocking.suggestion: Line 152 reads "Render with that Environment's `overlay` and `spec.variables`". Use the Configuration model field paths consistently: "`spec.overlay` and `spec.variables`".

`--output FORMAT` says `text` is the default for every command that prints data. But `ruralz bundle render` defaults to a YAML stream and `ruralz bundle export openapi` to YAML (Output formats table). State that the default is per command, as the Output formats table gives it.

Several Planned cells in the authentication table read "Same" instead of a tag (lines 391 and 392). Write the tag out, for example "Planned (M1); 9902 Planned (M2)", so that every availability cell carries a Planned (Mx) tag as style guide section 4 requires.

Tech stack and libraries names the "CLI reference owner" as owner of OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-18, but this document lists the CLI framework as a non-goal. Say instead that this document owns the requirements it states under Open questions (nested nouns, generated completions, no global state), and that the choice waits for a researched catalog row (pack 7, Pending selections).
